comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C27, C28 regarding Arp2/3 requirement for contraction. Both evaluations find the evidence compelling and well-supported, with peer reviewers describing experiments as 'technically excellent' and OpenEval noting the rigorous temporal control design.

Perfect agreement on claims C6, C29-C32 regarding N-WASP specificity versus WASP. Both evaluations strongly support the differential roles, with peer reviewers confirming the authors 'prove their claims' and OpenEval highlighting the convergent evidence from multiple independent approaches.

Strong agreement on inner F-actin foci characterization (C33-C41), though OpenEval also evaluates C5 which is not explicitly mentioned in peer review. Both find the evidence well-supported, with peer reviewers accepting the link between contraction and actin foci, and OpenEval emphasizing the quantitative temporal correlation.

Perfect agreement on claims C42-C48 regarding actin foci origin and dynamics. Both evaluations accept the kymograph analysis and centripetal movement findings without methodological concerns, with peer reviewers confirming the data support foci formation from lamellipodia.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C55 regarding dynamic properties of actin foci. Both evaluations support the quantitative measurements of lifetime and speed, with peer reviewers praising the thorough image analysis and OpenEval highlighting the rigorous paired analysis design.

Strong agreement on NMII recruitment and organization (C56-C63), though OpenEval also evaluates C7 not explicitly mentioned in peer review. Both find evidence supported, with peer reviewers noting new data added in revision addresses coordination between N-WASP and NMII, and OpenEval noting the WKO result requires further investigation.

Perfect agreement on claims C64-C65 regarding blebbistatin experiments and NMII motor activity. Both evaluations accept this evidence, with peer reviewers explicitly mentioning this as important new data added in revision, and OpenEval emphasizing the mechanistic insight provided.

Perfect agreement on claims C8, C66-C71 regarding BCR density increases during contraction. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers describing the proposal as 'provocative' (acknowledging novelty), and OpenEval confirming the quantitative analysis methodology is appropriate.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C72-C80 regarding the inverse relationship between BCR density and phosphorylation. Both evaluations accept the biphasic relationship findings, with peer reviewers noting it contrasts with other receptor models, and OpenEval emphasizing the rigorous statistical analysis.

Perfect agreement on claims C10, C12, C81-C90 regarding Syk dissociation at high BCR densities. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers confirming the demonstration of Syk disassembly and signal attenuation, and OpenEval noting the mechanism remains somewhat speculative.

Perfect agreement on claims C11, C13, C91-C98 regarding SHIP-1 dissociation. Both evaluations accept that SHIP-1 dissociates more readily than Syk, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming both kinases and phosphatases are pushed out, and OpenEval noting this challenges existing sequential recruitment models.

Perfect agreement on claims C14-C15, the main integrative conclusions. Both evaluations strongly support the overall mechanistic model linking actin reorganization to signal attenuation, with peer reviewers calling the study 'important' and providing 'novel insight,' and OpenEval noting the model is well-supported though alternatives cannot be excluded.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding mechanistic speculation (C110-C112). Both evaluations classify these as speculative, with peer reviewers noting the molecular crowding hypothesis is 'interesting' but requires future work, and OpenEval explicitly stating these lack direct experimental support. OpenEval also evaluates C109 not mentioned in peer review.
